title: Manzie Campbell's lesson and Collier Shows comedians
summary: Years later, Campbell advised Jones not to repeat a mistake at the drums; Jones recalls Collier's Shows with Johnny Hudgins, Johnny Knox and Pigmeat.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Ringling Brothers, Barnum and Bailey and whatever you read about Ringling Brothers, Barnum and Bailey they have to have crack Johnson there in his picture, a black man. He looked like Jack Johnson. But the drummer I spoke about, nobody in the whole world has ever played that much drums, because I forgot that I had met the man and years later I did a faux pas. I made a boo-boo. I did something wrong and this man came several years later and sat down at the drums where I was playing and he said, 'Son, you might go far. Don't make that mistake no more.' And he told me how to learn how to play drums, because I was trying to emulate the popular drummers in the territory that I was in, because as far as I was concerned, this was my world. I wasn't going nowhere. When I got to Omaha, Nebraska, I had made it. I wasn't going to go nowhere. Now I have met peoples that have traveled the whole world. They've been over to Europe, Australia, they've been everywhere and they tried to tell me, but I knew. I was smarter than they were. Don't tell me nothing; I'm Chicken Little; and this man, Monzie Campbell, the greatest drummer that ever lived, any way you wanted it, because it come to my mind I saw him but I didn't realize
Who was he with, Jo, Mancy Campbell?

He was with Collier's Shows and it was impossible, see, 'cause he had people like Johnny Hudgins on that show. You couldn't get on that show. That was the greatest show and they never came up North. That was Collier and his two daughters. a different thing... ^ It was only in later years that they extended up through Canada, but I mean Mr. Collier had died, you see, and all those peoples, all those big peoples in there - Willie Too Sweet and all those peoples - and Johnny Knox who was one of the greatest comedians that ever lived - the only one that I'd ever compare with him - Johnny Knox was out of Detroit - John Mason was the natural. Everybody knew he was a natural; and nobody knew about Pigmeat. I knew Pigmeat when he was on carnivals and HINTON: Pigmeat Markham. JONES: nobody ever saw Pigmeat in New York, like They would see him in Philadelphia when he'd get in front of a chorus line. He would take on a chorus where the chorus girl was supposed to take the thing, you see. But back to the music -
